reason: Attacked and it held, with one claim in the evidence struck. Wording and lineation: terebess.hu/english/haiku/basho2.html carries the verse verbatim, 'As firmly cemented clam shells / Fall apart in autumn, / So I must take to the road again, / Farewell, my friends.', with these capitals and this terminal stop, introduced by 'As I stepped into the boat, I wrote:' at Ogaki. I checked that the page really is Yuasa and not another hand: its opening reads 'Days and months are the travellers of eternity. So are the years that pass by', which is Yuasa's, and the page credits Nobuyuki Yuasa, Penguin, 1966, reprinted 1996. The four-line rendering is Yuasa's habit for haiku in that volume, so the lineation is the edition's and not a transcriber's. The struck claim: the evidence says 'the work's last words are this verse', and that is not true of this edition. What follows the verse is Soryu's postscript, dated early summer of the seventh year of Genroku, 1694. The verse is Basho's own last verse, which is what the source line actually says, 'the closing verse at Ogaki', so the shipped text is accurate and only the evidence prose overreaches. Attribution and locator: correct; the pun is the Futami parting of the clam shell as he leaves Ogaki for Ise. Checks: shipped [] and near [] for the lineated form and for a run-together form; Basho at 1 for the year from month 1, not at cap, not banned. Scope and format: pre-1999, no scripture, no warning needed, 105 characters, leads with the name, no dash, no straight quote, ends in a full stop, verse kept as verse, tag Poetry. Two notes for the editor. The evidence's 'work's last words' sentence should be corrected before this goes into the record. And this line and 08-cfl-05 are both Nobuyuki Yuasa in one month, against the one-poem-per-translator practice recorded in the Li Bai carry-in note, so one of the two should give way. Not refuted.
